## Now

M.S. candidate in Psychology: Data Science in Human Behavior at UW–Madison (expected Dec 2026). My capstone, **Digital-Mailroom**, is built with industry partner American Family Insurance. It looks for ways to cut the cost of AI inference and improve how documents are read, sorted, and managed.

## Featured Projects

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
### [Digital-Mailroom](projects/digital-mailroom.qmd)
[Capstone · American Family Insurance]{.kicker}

Five Python packages and one LangGraph pipeline that joins legal-document routing, prompt experiments, deterministic scoring, and deployment, in a reproducible Docker environment.
:::

::: {.card}
### [Mailroom-ML](projects/mailroom-ml.qmd)
[Training, evaluation & calibration]{.kicker}

A calibrated ModernBERT classifier that handles routine documents itself and sends uncertain ones to an LLM. Primary serving is ONNX on CPU. A Modal app is the fallback.
:::

::: {.card}
### [RVL-CDIP-Classifier](projects/rvl-cdip-classifier.qmd)
[Vision LLMs & prompt engineering]{.kicker}

Zero-shot document classification with vision LLMs: 29 tracked prompt versions, accuracy checked on larger slices than the tuning set, and the cost of every page measured.
:::

::: {.card}
### [Wave Laboratory](projects/wave-laboratory.qmd)
[Side project · simulation & graphics]{.kicker}

A real-time 3D ocean and ship-motion sandbox that runs in the browser, built on spectral wave physics.
:::
:::

## What I'm interested in

I'm interested in AI systems that know when they are unsure. That means calibrated classifiers, evaluation you can trust, and pipelines that pass hard cases to a stronger model or a person instead of guessing. Outside of that, I like turning physics into interactive software, and I'm interested in how people think, which is what my psychology training is about.
